items.title: We Built Our Website with Claude Code with no Human interaction
items.why_it_matters: A team built their entire company website using only Claude Code. It shows how far you can push the vibe-coding style of development when you focus on directing rather than typing. Try this week: Open Claude Code and prompt it to build a brand new, fully styled landing page for your AI-ingest project from scratch in one go.

items.title: Show HN: I rewrote Decap CMS with < $1K in Claude tokens
items.why_it_matters: An indie developer successfully rewrote an entire open-source content management system using less than $1,000 in Claude tokens. It proves you don't need a massive budget or a large team to execute complex, large-scale code refactoring. Try this week: Use Claude Code to refactor a messy component in your Next.js app, setting a strict token budget of $5 to see how much you can clean up.

items.title: I gave Claude Code and KimiCode shared memory so they stop forgetting my project
items.why_it_matters: A developer built a shared memory system for Claude Code to stop the AI from forgetting project context and repeating mistakes during long sessions. This solves one of the biggest pain points of building complex apps with AI. Try this week: Create a simple MEMORY.md file in your AI-ingest repo and instruct Claude Code to read and update it at the start and end of every coding session.

items.title: Show HN: Wallfacer – A terminal session manager for Claude Code, and more
items.why_it_matters: Wallfacer is a terminal session manager designed specifically for Claude Code, allowing you to easily manage, save, and switch between multiple active AI coding sessions. This makes it much easier to multitask across different features of your project without losing your place. Try this week: Install Wallfacer from GitHub and use it to split your Next.js frontend work and Supabase backend work into two separate, organized Claude Code sessions.

items.title: Show HN: The Channels SDK – Bring Any Agent to Any Channel (Slack, MS Teams)
items.why_it_matters: The Channels SDK lets you easily connect any AI agent or backend to communication channels like Slack, MS Teams, or Discord. This is perfect for turning a local script or web app into an active, messaging tool. Try this week: Install the SDK in your Next.js project and use it to automatically send your daily AI-news brief directly to a private Discord or Slack channel.

items.title: Show HN: Hope, 1-on-1 AI Tutor for kids Grades 2-10 learning math
items.why_it_matters: Two indie developers launched Hope, an interactive AI math tutor for kids, built and shipped in just three months. It is a great example of a simple, highly interactive AI wrapper that focuses on user experience over complex custom models. Try this week: Look at their interactive UI flow and try building a simple, single-page interactive Q&A component in your Next.js app using Supabase to store user responses.

items.title: How to recover what you want from Claude sessions without restarting?
items.why_it_matters: This utility helps you recover specific code snippets and context from active Claude sessions without having to restart the terminal or lose your current chat history. It saves time and tokens when Claude gets stuck or goes off track. Try this week: Clone the repo and run the recovery script the next time Claude Code gets stuck in a loop during your AI-ingest development.

items.title: Show HN: Aident Loadout – connect Codex and Claude Code to real apps
items.why_it_matters: Aident Loadout is an open-source tool that connects Codex and Claude Code to real local applications, allowing your AI editor to interact directly with your browser or system. This helps bridge the gap between writing code and testing it. Try this week: Set up the SDK to let Claude Code automatically open your local Vercel development server and verify that your Next.js app compiles without errors.
